title: Settlement run against a ledger service
name: Ledger settlement client

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code enforces its time limits on calls to the ledger service? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
`post_transfer` retries a POST after a read timeout, and a read timeout does not tell the client whether the ledger applied the transfer. What makes that retry safe here?
choices: The client closes and reopens the connection before each retry, so the ledger sees a new request
Every attempt sends the same Idempotency-Key, which is the transfer_id fixed when the PendingTransfer was created
Only status codes of 500 and above are retried, and those never apply the transfer
The balance check runs again before each attempt and prevents a double debit

questions.prompt: `_request` passes `timeout=attempt_timeout` (a plain float) to `self._client.request`, while the client was built with a four-part `httpx.Timeout`. For that call, what is the effect on the connect and pool phases?
choices: They keep the 1.0s and 0.5s values from the client settings, because only the read phase is overridden
They are disabled, so only the overall read time is limited
They also use attempt_timeout, replacing the stricter 1.0s connect and 0.5s pool limits with up to 4s
The call raises a TypeError because a float cannot override a Timeout object

questions.prompt: A batch of 200 transfers is started with a 20 second budget and the ledger becomes completely unreachable (every connection attempt fails fast). What does `SettlementRun.run` return?
choices: It raises LedgerUnavailable for the first transfer and the run aborts with nothing recorded
Each transfer is recorded as deferred after its own retries, and the run continues through the batch until it finishes or the budget runs out
All 200 transfers are marked insufficient because no balance could be read
The run hangs until the ledger recovers, since no overall timeout wraps the loop
